# LoomWeaver

> LoomWeaver is a domain-agnostic plugin & UI platform — the *loom* on which weavers (plugins) are woven into a product (a distribution). Domain UI runs as plugin bundles on top of it; the platform itself contains **zero domain logic** (a thin core that can only do plugins, the "actual app" is a first-party plugin bundle). A plugin ("weaver") consumes one uniform `ctx` contract from `@loomweaver/plugin-sdk`; a capability broker (**default-deny**) governs what each plugin may do. A product is a thin **distribution** that composes `@loomweaver/shell` + weavers from the published packages. Frontend: Angular + Nx. The platform ships **no server** — the backend seam (settings, auth, per-tenant secrets, egress) is the product's own backend, which implements the frontend ports (settings store / working-state store / `AuthSource`); the UI runs standalone with local/anonymous defaults. Status: the platform is **built and published** as seven versioned npm packages: `@loomweaver/plugin-sdk`, `@loomweaver/shell`, `@loomweaver/frame-kit` (UI assets for sandboxed plugins) and the scaffolding trio `@loomweaver/cli`, `@loomweaver/devkit` (Nx generators) and `@loomweaver/mcp` (an MCP server for AI assistants), plus `@loomweaver/ag-ui` (the AG-UI adapter, so an agent can reach the workbench's own commands).

This is a curated map for people — and their AI assistants — building on or integrating LoomWeaver. For a single-fetch brief with the complete contract inlined, see [`llms-full.txt`](llms-full.txt). Read from the repository, the links are repo-relative; served from loomweaver.dev, they are absolute.

## Start here

- [Glossary](docs/glossary.md): the words the docs use, one line each; platform, shell, host and workbench name the same thing.
- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): the mental model — platform / weaver / distribution, the uniform `ctx`, default-deny capabilities, the two RPC boundaries. Read this first.
- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): scaffold a running, branded product with a plugin already contributing to it, in ~5 minutes, using `@loomweaver/cli`.
- [Manual setup](docs/manual-setup.md): the same app wired by hand (~15 min) — the shell renders INSIDE the generated `app-root`, so nothing of `ng new`/Nx is deleted and every provider has one address (`src/app/app.config.ts`). Also the Nx differences (`project.json`, `@source` depth, `@loomweaver/devkit`), SSR (`RenderMode.Client`), and why Module Federation is not the plugin transport.
- [Samples](docs/samples.md): complete copyable recipes — a sidebar view with persisted `VIEW_STATE`, a routable surface with a `:param`, one command behind a shortcut + bar button + menu entry, a settings section, access gating, a confirm/progress/toast flow, and the full `VIEW_STATE` treatment (filter, active sub-tab, expanded nodes, scroll position in one shape) next to the counter-example that loses all of it. Each compiles against the published contract. The page opens by naming which recipes the generator already writes (a sidebar view, a routable surface, a command with its triggers, a settings section, access gating — one composed `weaver` call) so an assistant scaffolds them rather than typing them; recipes 6 to 10 are the hand-written remainder.

## Build

- [Authoring a weaver](docs/authoring-a-weaver.md): the shape of a weaver (manifest, `activate(ctx)`, where snippets go) and the map of the how-to pages, one task each:
  - [Surfaces in a sidebar](docs/weaver/sidebar-surfaces.md): a docked surface, and the custom-element escape hatch.
  - [View state that survives](docs/weaver/view-state.md): `VIEW_STATE`: filter, sub-tab, scroll position in one shape.
  - [Unsaved changes](docs/weaver/unsaved-changes.md): `DirtySurface` and the Save, Discard, Cancel question.
  - [Your plugin's own store](docs/weaver/plugin-state.md): `ctx.state`.
  - [Containers](docs/weaver/containers.md): a workspace in a tab, a child per item, relative addresses, pop-outs.
  - [The content area](docs/weaver/content-area.md): routable surfaces, tabs per pane, chromeless, closable, preview and pinned tabs, panes and tab groups.
  - [Sub-routes and follows](docs/weaver/sub-routes-and-follows.md): `subRoutes`, the rest of the address, tabs that follow the selection, `activeContent`.
  - [Context menus](docs/weaver/menus.md): `registerMenuItem`, item menu slots, `ctx.ui.openMenu`.
  - [Sandboxed surfaces](docs/weaver/sandboxed-surfaces.md): `component` or `iframe`, the sandbox bootstrap, the frame UI kit.
  - [Commands and their triggers](docs/weaver/commands.md): one behaviour behind shortcut, bar and rail items, palette and menu.
  - [Access gating](docs/weaver/access-gating.md): `access` on contributions and `ctx.session`.
  - [Icons and theme](docs/weaver/icons-and-theme.md): `ctx.contributeIcons`, `ctx.contributeTheme`.
  - [Host UI and host facts](docs/weaver/host-ui-and-facts.md): `ctx.ui` dialogs and toasts, `ctx.host`.
  - [Settings sections](docs/weaver/settings.md)
  - [Translations](docs/weaver/i18n.md)
- [Building a distribution](docs/building-a-distribution.md): the composition root (`app.config.ts`), which door a decision goes through, the composition report (`loomweaver.report()`), and the map of the how-to pages, one decision each:
  - [Layout](docs/distribution/layout.md): regions and docks.
  - [Content-area routing](docs/distribution/content-routing.md): `provideShellRouter`, following tabs.
  - [Workspaces](docs/distribution/workspaces.md): `provideWorkspaces`, an unusable workspace, telling saved ones apart.
  - [Resetting](docs/distribution/resetting.md): the reset control and what it asks.
  - [Switching capabilities off](docs/distribution/switching-capabilities-off.md): `provideShellFeatures`, the switch takes the gesture and the affordance.
  - [Surface retention](docs/distribution/surface-retention.md): the product-wide default.
  - [Branding](docs/distribution/branding.md)
  - [Capabilities](docs/distribution/capabilities.md): grants, default-deny, `provideRequiredPlugins`.
  - [Auth integration](docs/distribution/auth.md): `provideAuthSource`, your login UI, `provideUnauthorizedRedirect`.
  - [Persistence stores](docs/distribution/persistence.md): two ports of one shape, the storage-key inventory, identity-scoped stores.
  - [Windows and sync](docs/distribution/windows-and-sync.md): cross-tab live sync, pop-out windows.
  - [Frame plugins](docs/distribution/frame-plugins.md): `provideFramePlugins`, `@loomweaver/frame-kit`.
  - [Plugin store](docs/distribution/plugin-store.md): `providePluginCatalog`, runtime install, updates.
  - [Icons, translations and rewording](docs/distribution/icons-and-i18n.md): `provideIcons`, namespaces, `provideTranslationOverrides`.
  - [Recomposing host chrome](docs/distribution/recomposing-chrome.md): palette and quick-open entries, curating settings, dropping a route.
  - [PWA and delivery](docs/distribution/pwa.md)
- [Driving your product with an AG-UI agent](docs/ag-ui-agents.md): the path from `weaver --id <id> --agent` to a product an AG-UI agent drives — what the generator writes and what stays yours, the three things the panel makes visible (the offered list asked for again each run, arguments assembled from streamed fragments, an answer or an error worded so a refusal can be told from a failure), how to choose which calls get a confirmation (the `before` hook can only narrow: `run` means "no objection", never "make it reachable", and every refusal reads the same so nothing can be learned by probing), and that replacing the stand-in is one file. Read this before [agent tools](docs/reference/agent-tools.md), which is the adapter function by function.
- [The plugin system](docs/plugins.md): the distribution's view of plugins — the three rungs (trusted composed, sandboxed iframe over RPC, community-installed at runtime) against one contract, which parts of `ctx` cross the sandbox boundary and which stay trusted-only (a sandboxed surface may now be **docked** or a **container**, not only a content tab; `access` stays rejected), default-deny capabilities, what the user may revoke/disable/uninstall, the activation and respawn lifecycle, and the contribution-id collision trade.
- [Backend integration](docs/backend-integration.md): the product hand-off — the platform ships no server; wire your backend behind **four seams**: the settings store (with the all-or-nothing `peek` rule that separates a local from a network store), the optional working-state store, `AuthSource`, and **translations** (swap Transloco's loader to serve bundles from your API; the initial language is read from `localStorage` before DI, and a language beyond the shipped English/German is taken over wholesale).

## Concepts

Why the workbench behaves as it does; short, each linking to the how-to pages that act on it.

- [Surfaces and panes](docs/concepts/surfaces-and-panes.md): one contract for everything shown; a pane is a tab group.
- [The address](docs/concepts/the-address.md): one pane carries it; what has none.
- [Retention and unsaved work](docs/concepts/retention-and-unsaved-work.md): destroyed when clean; the question is asked by the action.
- [Capabilities and trust](docs/concepts/capabilities-and-trust.md): default-deny, three rungs, access is not a capability.
- [Workspaces](docs/concepts/workspaces.md): a whole way of working, its baseline, two origins.

## The contract — public API

- [`@loomweaver/plugin-sdk` public API](platform/libs/core/plugin-sdk/src/index.ts): everything a plugin imports (nothing else is public API).
- [Plugin contract](platform/libs/core/plugin-sdk/src/lib/plugin.ts): `Plugin`, `PluginManifest`, `PluginContext` (the `ctx` a plugin holds), `PluginUi` (`ctx.ui`), `PluginHost` (`ctx.host`), `PluginSession` (`ctx.session`).
- [Capabilities](platform/libs/core/plugin-sdk/src/lib/capability.ts): the coarse capabilities a plugin *declares* and a distribution *grants* — default-deny (`contributions`/`ui`/`host`/`navigation`/`session`/`theme`/`automation`).
- [Access gating](platform/libs/core/plugin-sdk/src/lib/auth.ts): `AuthSnapshot`, `AccessRequirement`, and the pure predicates — how a contribution reacts to login state + roles. Distinct from capabilities: what a *user* may see vs. what a *plugin* may do.
- [Worked example — the testbed weaver](platform/libs/weavers/testbed-weaver/src/lib/plugin/testbed.plugin.ts): a real in-repo plugin (dogfood). All domain content lives in a weaver like this, never in the core.
- [`loom-testbed` composition root](platform/apps/loom-testbed/src/main.ts): a worked distribution — `provideShellRouter` / `provideLayout` / `providePlugins` / `provideCapabilityGrants` / branding.

## Scaffolding & tooling (AI-assisted setup)

Deterministic scaffolding + validation for building on LoomWeaver. Prefer these over hand-wiring.

- [Scaffolding](docs/scaffolding.md): the guide — which of the three adapters applies to you, what the tools return, and every weaver option.
- [`@loomweaver/devkit`](platform/libs/tooling/devkit/README.md): the **Nx generator collection** — install as a dev dependency (`npm i -D @loomweaver/devkit`). The fullest adapter: Nx hands it a virtual tree, so it is the only one that also *changes* files (registers the project, adds the tsconfig alias). Placement is read from the workspace, not assumed — `--directory`, `--import-path` (defaults to your root manifest's npm scope), `--app` (inferred when there is exactly one application, an error naming the candidates when there are several), `--tags`, `--prefix`, `--unit-test-runner`. Generators — `weaver` (feature-composable: `--command`/`--shortcut`/`--menu`/`--bar-item`/`--settings`/`--about`/`--instanceable` [docks the surface — named instances exist only for a non-routable one]/`--container` [ nested pane tree at `<id>/:id`; mutually exclusive with `--instanceable`]/`--agent` [emits the AG-UI connection: a docked panel, the seam that decides about a call before it runs, and a local stand-in speaking the protocol so the whole path works on the first serve; implies `--command`, derives `automation`, and records `@loomweaver/ag-ui` + `@ag-ui/core`]/`--access`), `frame-plugin` (framework-agnostic iframe), `distribution` (runnable app; `--styles precompiled` emits a one-line stylesheet importing our pre-compiled `shell.css`, so the app needs **no Tailwind** — default `tailwind` compiles the source theme), `auth-source` + `settings-store` (backend ports), `theme` (`--preset bootstrap` maps all 29 `--lw-*` tokens onto Bootstrap 5.3's `--bs-*`), `layout`. E.g. `nx g @loomweaver/devkit:weaver --id=notes --settings --about`. Generated test wiring is `@nx/angular:unit-test` (Vitest); a weaver library compiles its specs with the build options of the app that `--app` resolves, and its i18n bundle is served through that app via a generated assets glob. Plus pure cores: `generate(recipe, input) → FileMap` and `validateManifest`/`validateI18nParity`.
- [`@loomweaver/cli`](platform/libs/tooling/cli/README.md): the scaffolding **CLI** — the primary path for a product repo, because it needs no Nx workspace, no LoomWeaver checkout and no assistant: `npx @loomweaver/cli weaver --id notes --command --shortcut 'mod+shift+n' --out src/lib/notes`. Same generators as MCP over the same pure core, so output is identical; it is the adapter that writes the files itself. `--dry-run`, `--force` (an existing file otherwise stops the run), `--strict` (validation warnings fail the exit code, for CI); as the writing adapter it refuses paths escaping `--out`, replaces symlinks rather than following them, and fails on an unknown flag. Also `validate-manifest`, `validate-i18n --dir <dir>` and `validate-catalog --file <path>` (the plugin store catalog is parsed defensively by the host — unknown fields, malformed values and whole entries disappear silently, so the validator names each consequence).
- [`@loomweaver/mcp`](platform/libs/tooling/mcp/README.md): an MCP server exposing the same scaffolding + validation as tools (`scaffold_*` return a file map; `validate_*` return findings) for AI assistants — transport-neutral core, stdio now. Published as a self-contained bundle, so a product repo that already consumes `@loomweaver/*` registers it in `.mcp.json` with `{ "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@loomweaver/mcp"] }` and gets scaffolding without a local devkit checkout (see its README).

## Distribution API

- [Distribution API](docs/distribution-api/index.md): every runtime service a distribution may inject — `DialogService`, `NotificationService`, `SettingsService`, `CommandService`, `AuthContext`, `ContentTabsService`, `PaneService` (the arrangement of the content area, panes addressed by opaque handles), `WorkspaceService` and `AppResetService` (guarded resets that answer whether they ran), `SidebarService`, `FeatureSwitches` (the capability switches, live and readable), `FontScaleService`, `PluginStoreService`, `UpdateService`/`VersionService`, `PopoutService`, `StateSyncService`, the plugin-management services — plus contributing chrome without a plugin (`provideViews`/`provideBarItems`/`provideRailItems`). The rule behind them: a switch removes the user's control, never the capability; every service action is the same code the control runs, with the same unsaved-work guards; facts are signals. A plugin never injects these; it goes through the brokered `ctx`.

## Platform reference

- [Shell anatomy](docs/reference/shell-anatomy.md): the region vocabulary (rail / panel / bar / content) and docks a distribution declares.
- [Callable commands](docs/reference/callable-commands.md): opening a command to a caller that is not the user — described `arguments` (a closed set of kinds), an `answers` declaration, a `description` written for something choosing between actions, and `callable` (opt-in, like `popout`). `ctx.invokeCommand` answers a refusal instead of throwing one; `ctx.invocableCommands()` is the workbench's own already-narrowed account, so nobody keeps a second list. Reaching another plugin's command needs the `automation` capability; your own need no grant.
- [Agent tools](docs/reference/agent-tools.md): `@loomweaver/ag-ui` — the adapter that describes the workbench's own commands to an AG-UI agent as tools and runs what it asks for through the same seam every other trigger uses. Headless: no transport, no UI, no agent. `commandTools(ctx)` gives `list()` (ask each run, never keep it) and `receive(event)`; a `before` hook may run, decline or answer a call itself, and can only narrow. An answer becomes the result's content, a refusal and a failure become `error` worded so they can be told apart, and every refusal reads the same whatever the reason so an agent cannot map what is installed by probing.
- [Access gating](docs/reference/access-gating.md): the complete `access` reference — the `AuthSnapshot`/`AccessRequirement` vocabulary (`claims` is carried but never matched), which surface reacts how to `hide`/`disable`, gated routes and the placeholder twin, the three readers of the session, the `onIdentityChange` policy, and why capability grants and access gating are orthogonal.
- [Routing](docs/reference/routing.md): the content area **is** the Angular router — `provideShellRouter()` wraps `provideRouter()`, contributed `routable` surfaces become ordinary `Route` objects once plugins have activated, and `routerLink`/`router.navigate`/`ActivatedRoute`/`<router-outlet>`/query params all behave normally. You write no `Routes` array for content and attach no `canActivate` of your own (`access` gates instead). Every navigation behaves the same, whoever started it: it reaches a pane that already holds the content instead of duplicating it, and is refused inside a pop-out — so `ctx.navigateContent` is not a behavioural alternative to a link, it is the capability-gated form a sandboxed plugin has and the one that reports back. Non-content routes go to `provideShellRouter([...])`. Two off-router cases: a `retain`ed surface (fabricated route — params only, never with `subRoutes`) and a pop-out (`routeConfig === null`).
- [Design tokens & `<lw-*>` vocabulary](docs/reference/design-tokens.md): the semantic tokens and host UI building blocks to use inside plugin templates (never raw palette colors). The vocabulary is **colour and type only** — sizes, radii and spacing have no tokens by decision; a product that must change one writes plain **unlayered** CSS, which beats everything the shell paints because all of it lives in cascade layers.
- [Icons](docs/reference/icons.md): every icon name `<lw-icon>` resolves out of the box, each with its glyph and the Heroicons export behind it, generated from the shell's own icon map. Names are semantic (`search`, not `magnifying-glass`), an unregistered name renders nothing, a weaver adds its own with `ctx.contributeIcons` (first-wins, never takes a name that exists) and a distribution with `provideIcons` (may replace a shipped glyph everywhere, sandboxed surfaces included).
- [Accessibility](docs/reference/accessibility.md): the WCAG 2.1 AA guardrail the host meets and weavers inherit.
- [`@loomweaver/shell` — the neutral host chrome](platform/libs/core/shell/README.md): renders regions and holds contributions; domain-pure.

## Packages

Seven npm packages, one shared version: `@loomweaver/plugin-sdk`, `@loomweaver/shell`, `@loomweaver/mcp` (the AI-scaffolding MCP server), `@loomweaver/cli` (the scaffolding CLI — same generators, driven by flags instead of an assistant), `@loomweaver/devkit` (the Nx generator collection), `@loomweaver/frame-kit` (static UI assets — the `<lw-*>` element bundle, compiled `.lw-*` CSS and Penpal — a distribution serves under `/frame-kit/` for sandboxed plugins), `@loomweaver/ag-ui` (the AG-UI adapter — the workbench's own commands offered to an agent as tools, headless). (No server packages — the platform is frontend-only.)

## For AI assistants

- [`llms-full.txt`](llms-full.txt): the complete contract (interfaces + provider signatures) and canonical distribution/weaver code, inlined for single-fetch ingestion.
- [Brand assets](assets/brand/): logo and colors (blue `#2E96C9`, gold `#C59A2F`).
